recorded.prompt:q-salt: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-salt: Page: "Python salts the hashes of strings: each process mixes a random value into hash() of every str and bytes, so the hash of the same string is the same within one process but different in the next." and "This is the morning analyst's story: two processes, two salts, two orders, two lists of 33." Output: set-order runs give "result.plan_digest differs".
recorded.prompt:q-clock: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-clock: "Under the clock the number of simplex iterations ... differs from run to run: each run stopped at a different point of the same path. Whether the plan differs too depends on whether a better plan turned up between those stopping points ... some runs of it returned one plan three times and others returned different plans; nothing about a clock limit makes either outcome reliable."
recorded.prompt:q-ties: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-ties: "any two plans that fund 33 projects are equally good, and the solver may return any of them" and "HiGHS and CP-SAT, each perfectly repeatable in the given order, return different plans from each other (e47f42d78207 and 7485409b35c7): a change of solver is a change of inputs too."

recorded.prompt:q-salt:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-salt:a: "A set's iteration order depends on the hashes of its items, and Python salts the hashes"; with ids unchanged, list(set(ids))[:5] was ['P002', 'P028', ...] under seed 1 and ['P016', 'P040', ...] under seed 2.
recorded.prompt:q-salt:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-salt:b: Reference table: "set iteration order | depends on the hashes, so on the salt; Python promises no order". The printed list(set(ids)) orders are not the order the ids were added.
recorded.prompt:q-salt:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-salt:d: The cause the page gives is the hash salt, not the solver seed. CP-SAT ran with "one worker, a fixed seed" and still showed "plan_digest differs" in set order, and 10.2.2 says HiGHS's "random_seed (default 0)", not a new seed per process.
recorded.prompt:q-clock:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-clock:a: Same passage: a matching plan under a clock limit is not reliable. 10.2.4 adds: "A clock-limited run that happened to return the same plan still shows different iteration counts ... keeping them makes the manifest stricter than the plan alone."
recorded.prompt:q-clock:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-clock:c: With the same settings, the node-limit run repeated: "Under the node limit ... every number repeats, iterations included." So the seed was not varying. The difference comes from the clock limit: "how many steps fit in 3 seconds depends on how busy the machine is."
recorded.prompt:q-clock:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-clock:d: The page blames the clock: "each run stopped at a different point of the same path", and the node-limit runs repeated every number. 10.2.2 adds: "The thread count changed nothing on this model: one thread, four threads and HiGHS's own choice all gave the seed-1 run."
recorded.prompt:q-ties:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-ties:a: "Every run proves 33 optimal." The model has tied optima, so two proofs need not agree on a list. 10.2.3: "At least 20 plans fund 33 projects."
recorded.prompt:q-ties:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-ties:b: HiGHS ran "with a zero gap tolerance, so each run proves its plan optimal", and the count is an integer, 33, in both.
recorded.prompt:q-ties:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-ties:c: One dataset gives many optimal lists: 10.2.3 says "At least 20 plans fund 33 projects", and this page says "The board's question has many answers."
